messages.author: 48e8abd2cd5ecdcd
messages.subject: Possible roxygen2 4.0.0 bug?
parts:
Hello,

I think I found a bug in the latest version of roxygen2 (4.0.0). I'm running R 3.1.0 on Windows.

I'm writing a package that uses figures in the documentation and I do so by following the answer in http://stackoverflow.com/a/7953949. That answer points to http://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/R-exts.html#Figures that says "http://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/R-exts.html#Figures".

If you create that folder, the new version of roxygen2 tries to access and modify the folder as a file and throws an error. For example,

> upgradeRoxygen()
Error in file(con, "r") : cannot open the connection
In addition: Warning message:
In file(con, "r") : cannot open file './man/figures': Permission denied

It looks like folders should be excluded from roxygen functions, if this is really a bug.

Alternatively, is there a preferable way to include images?

Thanks in advance,
Eduardo

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Possible roxygen2 4.0.0 bug?
parts:
Hi Eduardo,

upgradeRoxygen() has been done away with in the latest dev version, so
this should no longer be a problem. (upgrades now happen automatically
because I figured out a safer way to do it)

Hadley

messages.author: 48e8abd2cd5ecdcd
messages.subject: Re: Possible roxygen2 4.0.0 bug?
parts:
Mmm, it might be a Windows-only error. The development version does not work either.

I found that the error originates in the first line of "first_time" (https://github.com/klutometis/roxygen/blob/master/R/safety.R#L2). The dir() function will return a list of both files and directories (at least in Windows), as shown below in item number 4:

> dir("man", full.names = TRUE)
[1] "man/calculate_elcc.Rd"    "man/calculate_metrics.Rd" "man/capacity_value.Rd"   
[4] "man/figures"              "man/format_timedata.Rd"   "man/outage_table.Rd"     
[7] "man/repra.Rd"             "man/sliding_window.Rd" 

I am sending a pull request with the following lines that takes folders out of generated. An alternative would be to use a filter in dir().
generated <- generated[file.info(generated)$isdir]

Thanks,
Eduardo

On Friday, May 9, 2014 11:39:18 AM UTC-6, Hadley Wickham wrote:
It seems to be - I couldn't recreate the error.

Hadley
